sentences.text: As worded the premise is false: fiscal 2026 revenue grew 65.5%, which left it $45.06B short of the level a doubling required.
The doubling the thesis describes belongs to the two years before, at +125.9% and +114.2%; fiscal 2026 is the year growth slowed, by 48.7 percentage points.
The claim still points at something real on a different basis: the newest quarter's revenue grew 105.9% on a year earlier, but that is one quarter of fiscal 2027, not fiscal 2026.
The implications of a doubling also fail in fiscal 2026: neither operating income nor operating cash flow doubled, and receivables grew faster than revenue.

For a buy decision, the step from growth to price runs through the reverse DCF at the 2026-09-30 price, which needs only 13.4% a year for 10 years, so a doubling is not what the price requires. That figure leans most on a 65.2% operating margin held every year, and 0 of 40 ten-year spans of filers of this size grew that fast.
The record cannot say whether the quarter's 105.9% pace lasts through fiscal 2027, or what happened after the newest filing. The full fiscal 2027 10-K is the evidence that would tell.
Even at 65.5%, the growth came almost entirely from Data Center, at +60.2 percentage points, and ranked 6 of 63 among SIC 3674 filers, where the median was 13.0%.
Deferred revenue rose 215.1% against revenue's 105.9%, so billings ahead of delivery are growing faster than recognized sales, which is consistent with the quarterly reacceleration.

Among filers with revenue of at least $100.00B, a doubling held in 0 of 366 company-years. Among SIC 3674 filers, only 3 of the 12 readable cases held a year later, so the base rates make repeating the quarter's pace unusual.
Part of the newest quarter's growth is uncollected: receivable days rose to 59.6 from 54.1, with receivables up 126.8% against revenue's 105.9%.
The fiscal 2026 corollary on receivables points the same way, so collection lagged sales on both the annual and the quarterly basis.
The claim turns on the basis it is read on: on the fiscal year it fails by $45.06B, while on the newest quarter growth exceeds 100%.
For the decision, what matters is less whether revenue doubled than whether the 65.2% operating margin underlying the 13.4% implied growth holds.

conditions.text: A restated fiscal 2026 revenue at or above the $260.99B the doubling required would reverse the verdict.
An 8-K accounting item restating fiscal 2026 or fiscal 2025 revenue would change the base the test is computed on.
